articleTitle: Neural Network-Based Human Detection Using Raw UWB Radar Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: Ultra-Wideband (UWB) radar technology is a widely used technology for human detection and tracking through walls, because of its effectiveness in low-visibility situations. This study demonstrates a neural network-based identification of human presence using raw data obtained directly from the UWB radar. First, measurements have been collected with different human subjects at different positions relative to the UWB radar. A convolutional neural network (CNN) model has been trained on this dataset, to detect the presence of a human. Next, the algorithm effectiveness is deeply investigated using the Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) method, and the observations on detected presence are discussed.

articleTitle: Development of Crossover-Free 8 × 8 Butler Matrix for 2.4 GHz Beamsteering Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: In this paper, a crossover-free $8 \times 8$ Butler matrix is developed for 2.4 GHz beamsteering applications. The design aims to address the limitations of conventional $8 \times 8$ Butler matrices, which suffer from significant insertion losses and large physical dimensions due to the excessive use of crossovers. By eliminating crossovers, the proposed $8 \times 8$ Butler matrix achieves a more compact design with improved phase alignment and reduced insertion loss. The design is deployed on an FR4 Epoxy substrate with the dielectric constant of 4.3 and the thickness of 0.8 mm. The total size of crossover-free $8 \times 8$ Butler matrix takes 178.6 mm by 137.8 mm, representing a 55.4% size reduction compared to the conventional one. The results show that the reflection coefficients for all inputs and isolated ports are under $-\mathbf{2 0 ~ d B}$, and the insertion loss at the output port ranges between -10 dB and -11 dB, nearing the theoretical prediction of 9 dB. Furthermore, the proposed $8 \times 8$ Butler matrix achieves the fractional bandwidth of 13.75% at Port 1 and 25.4% at Port 4, indicating its wideband characteristics. In addition, the design of crossover-free $8 \times 8$ Butler matrix offers significant size reduction and improved performances, making it suitable for compact beamsteering antenna array applications.

articleTitle: Switchable Polarization Conversion Using Reflective Electromagnetic Surfaces in mmWave Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: In this paper, the design of a wideband switchable polarization conversion (SPC) is proposed by utilizing Reflective Electromagnetic Surfaces (RES) to operate in millimeter-wave (mmWave) spectrum. The SPC or polarizer which aims to work at two-state conditions comprises an infinite array of square patch unit cell in two-dimensional arrangement on an FR4 epoxy dielectric substrate. In the OFF-state condition, the proposed RES works as a polarizer, changing the linear polarization of incident waves into the circular polarization of reflected waves in the frequency range of 16 GHz to 25.5 GHz. Whilst in the ON-state condition, the RES functions as a regular reflector in the same frequency range. Characterizations using oblique incident waves show the influence of incident waves angle on the bandwidth response of RES as a polarizer. For every 10° increase in the angle of incident waves, the bandwidth response of polarizer decreases by about 5%.

articleTitle: A Novel AI Framework for WBAN Event Correlation in Healthcare: ServiceNow AIOps approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: Wireless Body Area Networks (WBANs) are one of the most innovative and advanced sensor networks that are revolutionizing healthcare monitoring; however, effective monitoring and correlating real-time physiological data streams are challenging. We present a new AI-driven framework using the ServiceNow AIOps platform to handle the aforementioned challenges. Using WBAN infrastructure applications, the proposed framework can handle different data streams in real time. Our framework identifies, categorizes, and prioritizes health incidents using rule-based filtering and advanced machine learning approaches. The ServiceNow platform’s event correlation engine can recognizes critical patterns and relationships among events, logs, and alerts and enables early detection, proactive intervention, and preemptive notification. With this integration, the platform receives multiple types of health data and analyzes, groups, classes, and responds to actionable events based on advanced analytics and predictive intelligence algorithms. A systematic approach was used to measure and analyze crucial success factors, such as the accuracy of event detection and the response time. The findings indicate that ServiceNow AIOPS can significantly enhance the capabilities of WBANs in terms of event correlation. Notable improvements were observed in the event detection accuracy and response times compared to traditional standalone monitoring systems. The platform’s adaptability to different WBAN sensor configurations and its scalable architecture are key advantages. In addition, the integration of machine learning algorithms augments the predictive intelligence capabilities, thereby reducing health event response times and enhancing overall reliability. The proposed research substantially contributes to the field by addressing the existing challenges in real-time WBAN monitoring, particularly in dynamic and data-intensive environments.

articleTitle: Development of Quadrifilar Conical-Helix Antenna for WLAN Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: This paper deals with the development of a quadrifilar conical-helix antenna intended to operate at the frequency of $2.4 \mathbf{G H z}$ in the Industrial, Scientific, Medical (ISM) bands for Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) communication. The proposed antenna comprises four copper wires which are wound three times around each other. A 50- $\Omega$ SMA connector is used to excite the antenna and connected to a micro strip feeding network deployed on an FR4 epoxy dielectric substrate. The conical shape of quadrifilar helix antenna is obtained by varying the radius change in each turn. To achieve the desirable performance, optimizations are carried out for the antenna design through simulation. Based on the optimized design, the antenna is realized manually and experimentally characterized. The characterization results show that the antenna prototype can operate at the desirable frequency for WLAN communication with the bandwidth response tailored to the required specification.

articleTitle: A Coupler with Programmable Characteristic for Butler Matrix Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: This paper presents a coupler with programmable phase-difference characteristic implementable for Butler Matrix applications. To achieve the characteristics, capacitors are placed at each intersection of the series and parallel arms of a branch line-type coupler. To verify the concept, a 3-bit variable phase-difference coupler is designed and simulated to operate at the frequency of 2.4 GHz. By properly selecting capacitance combinations from a 0.3 pF to 2.3 pF capacitance range, the proposed coupler produced eight phase-difference states from -120° to -50° with 10° increments. The designed coupler exhibits good scattering parameter response for all states. The reflection magnitude is better than -10 dB in 290 MHz(12%) bandwidth from the frequency of 2.19 GHz to 2.48 GHz. In such a bandwidth, the transmission magnitude is within -3.1 dB and -4.7 dB, which corresponds to a 1.6 dB imbalance with the maximum isolation of -13.9 dB. The designed coupler is then implemented in a $4 \times 4$ Butler matrix feeding network by substituting conventional hybrid couplers. The Butler matrix constructed with the proposed coupler demonstrates an increase in the number of output phase-differences, small transmission imbalance, good match, and high isolation.

articleTitle: A Leaky-wave Antenna Based on Series-fed Patch Array with Semi-elliptical Arms for X band Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: This work proposes a leaky-wave antenna based on a series-fed patch array with semi-elliptical arms for X-band radar applications. The antenna uses series-fed patch unit-cells with elliptical arms as its leakage element to eliminate the open-stop band (OSB) problem and achieve continuous beam scanning. The antenna operates from 8 to 12 GHz with a beam-scanning range of -67° to 23°. Due to its maximum gain of 15 dBi, efficiency of over 75%, simple design, and ease of manufacture, it can be a practical choice for many wireless communication applications, including radar, remote sensing, and weather monitoring in the X-band.

articleTitle: Experimental Exploration of OTFS-Based 28 GHz UWB Pulsed Doppler Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) is a novel modulation system for wireless communication in which data symbols are allocated in delay-Doppler (DD) domain. OTFS is proposed for use in next-generation communication systems and one of its uses is also in radar technologies. In this paper, a preliminary setup of an OTFS-based ultra-wideband (UWB) pulse Doppler radar is presented with results obtained from the experiments. Implemented radar’s prototype transmits OTFS modulated pilot with the use of arbitrary waveform generator (AWG) and up-conversion to the 28 GHz carrier frequency. In the experiments, a static object at different distances from the radar system is detected with three delay resolutions. Results are represented in DD domain and are consistent with distances to the object. Radar’s measurements also show the connection between DD domain and range-velocity matrix, through simple conversions of axes.

articleTitle: A Leaky-wave Antenna Based on Series-fed Slotted Patch Array and Transverse Stubs for K Band Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: This paper presents a microstrip-based leaky-wave antenna for K-band radar, consist of a series-fed slotted patch with transverse stub leakage cells. The antenna achieves backward-to-forward beam propagation by incorporating slots into the conventional series patch design. The addition of transverse stubs between patches effectively resolves the resulting open-stopband (OSB) issue. Operating across 18.6 to 29.6 GHz, the antenna supports continuous beam scanning with a high efficiency averaging 85% and a wide beam-scanning range of -67° to 20°. It maintains a gain of 13 to 16 dBi within its the operating range. The proposed antenna shows great potential as a wireless communication element for air monitoring and next-generation K-band radar applications.

articleTitle: Parameter Adjustment of the Pompilio Propagation Model for Coastal RF Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: Requirements such as availability, reliability, and scalability are essential to achieve the stringent performance targets established for a radio link project. This work proposes a methodology for the parameterization and adjustment of a new propagation model called the Pompilio Propagation Model (PPM). This radio frequency (RF) propagation model is ideal for communication in coastal regions, utilizing the 4 and 5 GHz spectrum bands, and is implemented through a commercial computational tool for empirical RF prediction.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Quadrature Chaos Shift Keying Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: This study investigates the experimental implementation of the Quadrature Chaos Shift Keying (QCSK) communication system as a method to strengthen physical layer security in Internet of Things (IoT) communication. It highlights the critical function of chaotic oscillators in enhancing IoT security. A comprehensive analysis is provided, showcasing the potential of chaos oscillators in achieving reliable and secure data transmission. A QCSK communication system prototype using analog components was developed and evaluated experimentally to validate the system’s performance. The experimental setup included two configurations, emphasizing the importance of selecting appropriate signals for synchronization and information transfer. The system’s performance was measured using the bit error ratio as a key metric.

articleTitle: Evaluating Substrate Influence on Rectangular and Circular Microstrip Patch Antennas for 5G
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: Microstrip Patch Antennas (MSPAs) are favored for their low production cost, compact size, lightweight nature, and adaptability to planar and non-planar surfaces. They are particularly suitable for wideband and multi-frequency operations, making them ideal for sub-6 GHz applications in 5G devices. This study aims to design and compare rectangular and circular MSPAs using six different substrates: FR4 Glass Epoxy (dielectric constant 4.3), ROGERS DT5880 (2.2), ROGERS 4003C (3.3), Teflon (2.1), Arlon AD300A (3), and Alumina (9.9). Using CST Microwave Studio, we first design rectangular MSPAs and then circular MSPAs, maintaining a 1.6 mm substrate height and using Copper (Anneal) for both the patch and ground materials. The target frequency is 5.8 GHz, relevant for 5G applications. By comparing the antenna parameters across different substrates, we aim to identify the optimal substrate and antenna design for future technology needs.

articleTitle: Super Wideband Spearhead-Shaped Planar Antenna for EMC Testing and Radio Frequency Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental investigation on the performance characteristics of a super wideband (SWB) spearhead-shaped planar antenna designed for electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) testing and radio frequency surveillance applications. The proposed antenna features compact dimensions of $40 \mathrm{~mm} \times 50 \mathrm{~mm}$ and a broad operating bandwidth spanning from the frequency of 3.66 GHz to 43.5 GHz, making it a suitable candidate for various wireless communication systems. The low return loss value of proposed antenna over the entire frequency range of interest indicates its potency as a wideband sensor for EMC testing and radio frequency surveillance. The experimental investigation of antenna performance in EMC testing from the frequency of 1 GHz to 6 GHz demonstrates its ability to effectively detect emissions from devices under test that operate in the frequency bands of 2.4 GHz, 4 GHz, and 5.8 GHz. In addition, the proposed antenna is successfully implemented in radio frequency surveillance application, where it is capable of detecting the utilized frequency spectrum from the frequency of 1 GHz to 6 GHz in an environment encompassing aeronautical and satellite radionavigation, radiolocation, and fixed-and-mobile communication services, showing a good level of sensitivity. Keywords-Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) testing; radio frequency surveillance; super wideband (SWB) antenna; wideband sensor.

articleTitle: Wide Tuning Range X-Band LC-VCO Designed in 90 nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: This paper presents a wide tuning range LC-VCO with additional power down and differential-to-single circuits designed in 90 nm CMOS technology. Designed LC-VCO generates signal in widely used X-band frequency range. Post-layout simulated frequency is $7.97-11.53 \mathrm{GHz}$ reaching 36.44% frequency tuning range. Achieved simulated phase noise of ${- 1 1 1. 0 8 ~ d B c / H z}$ at 1 MHz offset from 7.976 GHz carrier frequency. The proposed VCO achieves FOM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf> of -183.07 dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: Discrete Sequential Implementation of Chaos Oscillators for FPGA Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: The current work focuses on implementing chaos oscillators in sequential logic form for the field-programmable gate array (FPGA) operation. The paper develops MATLAB models that emulate the dynamics of Vilnius and RC chaos oscillators in fixed-point arithmetic. The developed models are verified by performing Pecora-Carroll synchronization with the oscillator circuits. This study demonstrates that the developed models reflect the performance of chaos oscillators and the possibility of analog-discrete chaotic synchronization.

articleTitle: Characterizing Attenuation of Bumper Modifications: A Comparative Study in the E-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: Having knowledge about the attenuation of the materials surrounding a radar sensor is of great importance in the automotive sector. Only then can the manufacturer guarantee the desired functionality of the sensor. Due to the fact that a lot of automotive manufacturers also started integrating radar sensors behind rear bumpers for improved visibility to the back of a car, it is vital to know how those bumpers and possible repair scenarios done to them can affect the radar sensor. This paper proposes a way to measure the attenuation in the E-band of not only square slab samples representing various types of paint and repair scenarios on automotive bumpers, but also actual rear bumpers with different types of repair scenarios. The results are then presented and compared relative to each other.

articleTitle: Development of Dual-Band Microstrip Bandpass Filter Based on Dual-Mode Resonator for Wireless Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: This paper discusses the development of a dual-band microstrip bandpass filter (BPF) based on a dual-mode resonator implemented for wireless communication application. The proposed microstrip BPF is targeted to work at two frequency bands with the center frequencies of 1.575 GHz for Global Positioning System (GPS) L1 and 2.45 GHz for Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) communication applications. The filter is configured by two dual-mode resonators and two feed lines with each shape takes an imperfect ellipse. A 1.6 mm thick FR4 epoxy dielectric substrate with the dimensions of $\mathbf{6 8. 6} \mathbf{~ m m}$ $\times 37.2 \mathrm{~mm}$ is used for the design and realization. The optimized design is then realized for experimental measurement. The measured results of realized dual-band microstrip BPF have two frequency band responses, the first is at the center frequency of 1.575 GHz with the reflection coefficient ($S_{11}$) and transmission coefficient $\left(S_{21}\right)$ values of $-\mathbf{2 0. 9 6 9} \mathrm{dB}$ and -2.693 dB respectively, and the second is at the frequency of 2.525 GHz with the $S_{11}$ and $S_{21}$ values of -16.617 dB and -2.483 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Infrastructure and Regulation: Pillars of Reliability in 6G Networks with NR+
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: Reliability in transmission systems is a cornerstone for achieving excellence in 6G services. This paper delves into the critical role of reliability in delivering high-quality telecommunications services, focusing on the challenges and opportunities related to the implementation of the NR+ standard in Brazil. Conducted in partnership with the university, telecommunications market players, and the regulatory agency, this research utilized a solid case analysis to develop procedures that can be applied nationwide. The study underscores the importance of robust infrastructure, appropriate regulations, and effective reliability evaluation mechanisms to ensure service quality and customer satisfaction. Standardizing rules for all market participants, along with the use of key indicators such as the Service Quality Index (SQI), Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI), and Service Delivery Index (SDI), as well as the assessment of factors like network retention capacity and latency, are vital for the successful deployment of 6G in Brazil. Reliability, therefore, emerges as a fundamental pillar in building a connected future with high-quality services and significant socioeconomic benefits for the country.

articleTitle: Enhancing Classification Accuracy in Cooperative Spectrum Sensing Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: In this article, we evaluate the ability of three algorithms (k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN), Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis (PLSDA), and K-means Clustering) to detect spectrum holes. The research results indicate that kNN clustering and PLSDA outperform K-means clustering when considering the different distances between Secondary Users (SU) and Primary Users (PU). In scenarios with high energy transmission, PLSDA and kNN exhibit excellent performance, with PLSDA showing balanced performance indicators, making it an ideal choice for high-energy environments. Future research will focus on other Machine Learning (ML) techniques to further improve the accuracy of spectrum sensing in various scenarios.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Narrowband and Ultra-Wideband Systems for Device-Free Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: Setting up a device-free localization (DFL) system requires an appropriate selection of radio technologies and algorithms. The selection has impacts on the complexity of both, signal processing, and hardware infrastructure, as well as the maintenance effort. The radio technology has an impact on the system’s infrastructure as some localization algorithms demand extensive manual calibration, leading to increased maintenance efforts. To address these challenges, we developed and compared two DFL systems: one based on narrowband (NB) radio technology with received signal strength (RSS) measurements, and another with an ultra-wideband (UWB) radio chip with channel impulse response (CIR) measurements that enables utilization of multipath propagation. We evaluated both systems using a fingerprinting method and a radio tomographic imaging algorithm across various configurations. Our experimental evaluation demonstrates the differences in radio technologies and localization accuracy, and maintenance requirements, therefore provides help for developers of localization systems.

articleTitle: Finite state machine model checking of a wave-union-based TDC FPGA system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: This paper introduces the initial steps towards formal verification of a wave-union based time-to-digital converter (TDC) system designed in a field-programmable gate array (FPGA). Although a wave-union-based TDCs has demonstrated high single-shot precision (tens of picoseconds and even smaller), low dead time, and scalable reconfigurability, it presents significant implementation and calibration challenges due to its strong dependence on the low-level FPGA architecture and its parameters. This paper proposes model checking as the key initial method to verify the correctness of the wave-union-based system. Two finite state machiness (FSMs) were constructed: a reference FSM describing the operation in terms of hardware signals, and a more abstract implementation FSM based on logic assertions derived from the reference FSM. The state transitions were defined using linear temporal logic (LTL). The implementation FSM was analyzed in NuSMV model checker for deadlock-free operation. The result revealed loopback errors which may lead to potential deadlocks. Overall, the verification process demonstrated that the implementation FSM very effectively simulates the operation of a wave-union-based TDC system and can be used for more complex formal verification procedures, such as reachability analysis. This work lays the foundation for research into the formal verification of a wave-union TDC implemented in FPGA.

articleTitle: On Cyber Threats in Military Communication Nets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Workshop on Microwave Theory and Technology in Wireless Communications (MTTW)
abstract: The activities on cybersecurity were initiated by the GAO report 2018, which stated that the US weapons systems developed in 2012-2017 have severe cyber vulnerabilities. It was based on the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2014, the latest version 2.0 (2024). From the software point of view, we looked at the fate of four US weapons programs: (1) F-35 Lightning II aircraft. The F-35 Program software has more than 80 million lines of code. Despite 20 years and ${\$}$62.5 billion spent on R&D alone, there is not yet an answer - how to complete the F-35 Program; (2) Joint Tactical Radio System - the purpose to replace the 25 to 30 currently used military radio systems. After 15 years and ${\$}$15 billion, the JTRS program was canceled in 2011; (3) Single Security Architecture based on Joint Regional Security Stacks. In 2021 the Pentagon postponed this ${\$}$2 billion cybersecurity project; (4) Missile destroyer DDG 1000 (started 2006) is driven by 14 to 16 million lines of computer code. Cybersecurity and software architectures are the aim of this paper. CORBA technology was originally designed for RPC applications. It was a critical mistake. Instead of CORBA, nowadays there can be REST; GraphQL; Protocol Buffers; gRPC; microservices, etc.
